identity.title: Food Safety Plan — Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips (Salem Plant)
identity.issuer: Willamette Valley Foods, Inc. (internal document; prepared by PCQI Dana Whitfield, approved by Plant Manager)

scan.summary: This is the company's internally written FSMA food safety plan for its refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dip line, covering hazard analysis, preventive controls, monitoring, corrective actions, verification, supply-chain screening, records, and training. It is the document a plant is required to hold and follow under 21 CFR Part 117; it is not an agency permit, so the fixes below are things the company itself must add, not conditions imposed from outside.
scan.freshness_note: The plan is dated effective 2025-05-12, about 16 months old as of this review (2026-09-27). It does not itself state when it must be reanalyzed, so there is no internal 'renew by' date to check it against; under the rule governing it, a reanalysis is due at least every 3 years (around mid-2028) or sooner if the process changes.

gaps.title: No written recall plan
gaps.description: The plan identifies several hazards that require a preventive control (Listeria, sesame allergen, metal, pathogen survival at cook, spore-former growth at cooling) but contains no recall plan describing how consignees would be notified, when a public warning would be issued, how effectiveness checks would be done, or how recalled product would be disposed of.
gaps.fix: Add a recall plan section naming who leads a recall, how direct consignees (distributors/retailers in OR, WA, ID) are notified using the existing lot/date coding, the criteria for a public warning, the effectiveness-check method, and disposition options (rework, divert, destroy).
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.139(a), required as part of the plan under 21 CFR 117.126(b)(4)
gaps.locator: not in the document (would sit after section 8, before section 9 Records)

gaps.title: No documented validation of critical limits
gaps.description: Section 7 (Verification) covers calibration, record review, product testing, and trending, but nowhere does the plan show that the cook (212°F/60 min) or the two-stage cooling schedule were validated — e.g., against published thermal-lethality data or a challenge study — as adequate to control Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes, or spore-former outgrowth.
gaps.fix: Add a validation subsection citing the scientific or technical source (published data, challenge study, or recognized process authority) supporting each critical limit, signed by the PCQI.

gaps.title: No stated reanalysis interval
gaps.description: The plan does not commit to a reanalysis schedule. The rule requires reanalysis at least once every 3 years, and sooner if there is a significant change to the process, ingredients, or equipment, or new information about a hazard.
gaps.fix: Add a statement committing to reanalysis at least every 3 years from the effective date (by 2028) and whenever a significant change occurs, with PCQI sign-off recorded at that time.

gaps.title: Approval line lacks a name and a dated signature
gaps.description: The rule requires the owner, operator, or agent in charge to sign and date the food safety plan initially and upon any modification. The document only shows a title, with no personal name and no signature date distinct from the plan's stated effective date.
gaps.fix: Have the actual owner, operator, or agent in charge sign their name and date the approval line, and re-sign whenever the plan is revised.

gaps.title: Supply-chain program underspecified
gaps.description: Section 8 states only that tahini and dry beans come from approved suppliers with an audit certificate and certificate of analysis. It does not name who approves suppliers or on what criteria, why that particular verification activity (audit + COA) was chosen for the sesame allergen hazard and the physical-hazard risk in dry beans, the audit/COA review frequency, or a reanalysis commitment for the supply-chain program itself.
gaps.fix: Expand the supply-chain section to name the responsible party, the verification activity chosen per raw material and the reasoning, the review frequency, and a reanalysis commitment consistent with the supply-chain subpart.
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

deadlines.source_line: Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly

deadlines.source_line: the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually

deadlines.source_line: Finished product is tested for Listeria monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory

deadlines.source_line: Environmental monitoring results are trended quarterly

deadlines.source_line: All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually

deadlines.source_line: The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven working days of their creation

deadlines.source_line: All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed by the PCQI within seven days

facts.value: 28 production employees, one shift, five days a week, at Salem
facts.quote: The Salem plant operates one shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees.
facts.affects: Indicates scale of operation and the number of people covered by the annual hygiene-training requirement.

A 45-day refrigerated shelf life on an RTE product that supports Listeria growth is why weekly environmental swabbing and monthly finished-product testing are needed; it also raises the bar for how solid the cooling and sanitation preventive controls must be.

facts.quote: for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho
facts.affects: Interstate distribution places the facility under FDA's 21 CFR Part 117 jurisdiction in addition to Oregon Department of Agriculture oversight, and may bring in Washington/Idaho requirements for products sold there.

facts.value: PCQI (Dana Whitfield) completed FSPCA course in March 2024
facts.affects: Establishes the credential relied on for the person who must prepare or oversee the hazard analysis and plan under the preventive-controls-qualified-individual requirement.

expected_missing.why: A pest control program and log of service visits is a standard companion document at RTE food plants and is not referenced anywhere in this plan.
expected_missing.basis: similar companies, not a checked requirement

WILLAMETTE VALLEY FOODS, INC.
FOOD SAFETY PLAN
Ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips
Salem Plant, 1850 Fairgrounds Road NE, Salem, Oregon 97301
Effective date: May 12, 2025
Prepared by: Dana Whitfield, Quality Manager, Preventive Controls Qualified Individual
(PCQI certificate, FSPCA course, March 2024)
Approved by: Plant Manager
1. Facility and product description
Willamette Valley Foods produces refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dips in 8-ounce and 16-
ounce sealed plastic tubs for retail sale in Oregon, Washington and Idaho. The Salem plant operates one
shift, five days a week, with 28 production employees. Products are made from cooked chickpeas or black
beans, tahini, lemon juice, garlic, olive oil, salt and spices, blended, filled, sealed, coded and held
refrigerated at or below 41°F. Shelf life is 45 days refrigerated. Products are labeled with the allergen
statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.
2. Process flow
Receiving of dry beans, tahini and other ingredients → dry storage or refrigerated storage → soaking and
cooking of beans (kettle, 212°F, 60 minutes minimum) → cooling in the blast chiller → blending with
other ingredients → filling and sealing → date coding → metal detection → refrigerated storage →
shipping.
3. Hazard analysis

tahini contact with bean dips made without
tahini

beans (Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes) product

and Bacillus cereus spore-former outgrowth

storage shelf life

and ingredients
4. Preventive controls
Hazard Preventive control Type Critical limit or parameter
Vegetative Cook beans in the kettle to an internal temperature of at Process Minimum 212°F for 60 minutes, measured
pathogens at cook least 212°F for at least 60 minutes with a calibrated probe thermometer
Spore-former Cool cooked beans from 135°F to 70°F within 2 hours Process 135°F to 70°F in 2 hours; 70°F to 41°F in
growth at cooling and to 41°F within a further 4 hours in the blast chiller 4 hours
Listeria in the Sanitation of food-contact surfaces before each Sanitation ATP swab pass before start-up; Listeria
RTE environment production run and between products; environmental spp. swabs, 10 sites weekly, zone 1 and 2
monitoring swabs weekly
Sesame allergen Allergen labeling review for every label at receipt and at Allergen Label matches the formulation sheet;
printing; product scheduling with hummus items last in washdown verified by ATP swab before
the day, followed by full washdown the next non-sesame product
Metal Metal detection of every sealed tub Process Reject at 2.0 mm ferrous, 2.5 mm non-
ferrous, 3.0 mm stainless test pieces
5. Monitoring
The kettle operator records the internal temperature and the time at the start and end of each cook batch
on the cook log. The blast chiller operator records the temperature at 2 hours and at 6 hours on the cooling
log. The sanitation lead records the ATP swab result before each start-up. The line lead runs the three
metal test pieces through the detector at start-up, every two hours, and at the end of the run, and records
the result. The quality technician reviews every label lot against the formulation sheet at receipt and signs
the label log.
6. Corrective actions
If a cook batch does not reach 212°F for 60 minutes, the batch is re-cooked to the critical limit or
discarded, and the cause is recorded. If cooling exceeds the time limits, the batch is discarded. If an ATP
swab fails, the surface is re-cleaned and re-swabbed before production starts. If a Listeria spp. swab is
positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since
the last negative swab is held pending investigation. If the metal detector fails a test piece, all product
since the last passing test is re-run through the detector. If a label does not match the formulation, the lot
is quarantined and not used. All corrective actions are recorded on the corrective action log and reviewed
by the PCQI within seven days.
7. Verification
The PCQI reviews the cook, cooling, sanitation, allergen and metal detection records within seven
working days of their creation. Probe thermometers are calibrated in ice water and boiling water weekly,
and the metal detector is serviced by the manufacturer annually. Finished product is tested for Listeria
monocytogenes monthly by an accredited laboratory. Environmental monitoring results are trended
quarterly.
8. Supply-chain program
Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit
certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot. The approved supplier list is maintained by the quality
manager.
9. Records
All records named in this plan are kept at the Salem plant for at least two years from the date of the record
and are available to FDA and the Oregon Department of Agriculture on request. Records are reviewed and
signed by the PCQI as described in section 7.
10. Training
All production employees receive food hygiene training at hire and annually. The PCQI holds a current
FSPCA certificate. Sanitation and line leads are trained on the monitoring procedures in this plan.

soft.text: No documented validation of critical limits / Section 7 (Verification) covers calibration, record review, product testing, and trending, but nowhere does the plan show that the cook (212°F/60 min) or the two-stage cooling schedule were validated — e.g., against published thermal-lethality data or a challenge study — as adequate to control Salmonella, Listeria monocytogenes, or spore-former outgrowth. / Add a validation subsection citing the scientific or technical source (published data, challenge study, or recognized process authority) supporting each critical limit, signed by the PCQI. / 21 CFR 117.160 / https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-117/subpart-C/section-117.160 / not in the document (section 7, Verification) / read

No stated reanalysis interval / The plan does not commit to a reanalysis schedule. The rule requires reanalysis at least once every 3 years, and sooner if there is a significant change to the process, ingredients, or equipment, or new information about a hazard. / Add a statement committing to reanalysis at least every 3 years from the effective date (by 2028) and whenever a significant change occurs, with PCQI sign-off recorded at that time. / 21 CFR 117.170 / https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-117/subpart-C/section-117.170 / not in the document / read

soft.text: Supply-chain program underspecified / Section 8 states only that tahini and dry beans come from approved suppliers with an audit certificate and certificate of analysis. It does not name who approves suppliers or on what criteria, why that particular verification activity (audit + COA) was chosen for the sesame allergen hazard and the physical-hazard risk in dry beans, the audit/COA review frequency, or a reanalysis commitment for the supply-chain program itself. / Expand the supply-chain section to name the responsible party, the verification activity chosen per raw material and the reasoning, the review frequency, and a reanalysis commitment consistent with the supply-chain subpart. / 21 CFR 117.410–117.475 (Subpart G, Supply-Chain Program) / https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-B/part-117/subpart-G / page 6, section 8 / read / Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.
